evals.name: internal-repo-not-community-project
evals.prompt: Add a GOVERNANCE.md to the ledger-sync repo. It's one of our internal platform tools, maintained by the Platform Data team -- no public contributors, no elections, nothing like that. The repo is at the current directory.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as the internal/platform-repo case rather than defaulting to CNCF-style community-project scaffolding (elections, fixed terms, public meetings, a steering committee). Answers the three core governance questions (how roles are gained/lost, how decisions are made, how conflicts resolve) in a short, direct way appropriate to a single-team internal repo, naming a real escalation path (e.g. a tech lead or engineering manager) rather than inventing a formal voting procedure or committee that doesn't exist. Does not fabricate a specific manager/lead name that was never confirmed.

evals.name: steering-committee-for-small-project
evals.prompt: Can you set up a GOVERNANCE.md for my project, streamlit-widgets? I want to use a full steering committee with elections, like Kubernetes has. The repo is at the current directory.
evals.expected_output: Notices that the repo has a single maintainer and no sub-groups, working groups, or subprojects -- the specific condition CNCF reserves the Steering Committee/Elections model for. Pushes back on or questions applying a steering-committee/elections structure to a single-maintainer project before writing it verbatim, explaining that a committee/election structure with no real body behind it would misrepresent who has authority, rather than silently complying and producing a document describing elected officials and terms that don't exist for a one-person project.

evals.name: audit-stale-maintainer-council
evals.prompt: Can you audit our GOVERNANCE.md and tell me if it still matches how the project actually runs? Don't rewrite it, just tell me. The repo is at the current directory.
evals.expected_output: An audit report, not a rewrite -- GOVERNANCE.md itself is not modified. Correctly flags that GOVERNANCE.md lists a three-person Maintainer Council (including someone who, per CONTRIBUTING.md/CODEOWNERS, is no longer a maintainer) as stale/inaccurate. Treats this reality-mismatch as the top-priority finding, ahead of secondary structural observations.
